text: I am an executor handling probate and deceased estate administration in Brisbane Southside (Mount Gravatt & Sunnybank). Which law firms specialise in Queensland probate and estate administration?

result.markdown:
For an executor administering a deceased estate in Brisbane Southside, particularly around Mount Gravatt and Sunnybank, I’d focus on Queensland law firms that explicitly handle **probate, obtaining a grant of probate or letters of administration, executor advice, estate administration and distribution to beneficiaries**\.

It’s worth choosing a firm that acts for executors in their representative capacity, rather than one that primarily prepares wills. If the estate involves a property sale, disputes between beneficiaries, or complex tax and accounting issues, ask whether those services can be coordinated as part of the administration.

## How I would shortlist them

For your circumstances, I would seek initial quotes from **Elliott & Harvey, Ian W Bartels & Associates, and one dedicated succession-law firm such as Little Estate Lawyers or Direct Lawyers**\. That gives you a comparison between local convenience and specialist expertise without committing to the first firm you contact.

Before engaging anyone, ask these questions\:

- **Scope\:** Will you handle the entire estate administration, or just the probate application?
- **Costs\:** Can you provide a written estimate covering legal fees, court filing fees, searches, property transfers and disbursements?
- **Executor obligations\:** Will you advise me about debts, tax clearance, beneficiary entitlements and when it is safe to distribute the estate?
- **Property\:** Can you handle the transfer or sale of any Queensland real estate held by the deceased?
- **Complexity\:** Can you assist if a beneficiary challenges the will or makes a family provision claim?

You can also verify a solicitor's practising status and look for succession-law accreditation through the [Queensland Law Society](https://www.qls.com.au/)\.

**One important distinction\:** obtaining a grant of probate is only one part of the job. If you want help managing the estate from the initial asset and liability checks through to final distribution, make sure the engagement covers that broader work.

For your circumstances, I would seek initial quotes from **Elliott & Harvey, Ian W Bartels & Associates, and one dedicated succession-law firm such as Little Estate Lawyers or Direct Lawyers**\. That gives you a comparison between local convenience and specialist expertise without committing to the first firm you contact.

Before engaging anyone, ask these questions\:

- **Scope\:** Will you handle the entire estate administration, or just the probate application?
- **Costs\:** Can you provide a written estimate covering legal fees, court filing fees, searches, property transfers and disbursements?
- **Executor obligations\:** Will you advise me about debts, tax clearance, beneficiary entitlements and when it is safe to distribute the estate?
- **Property\:** Can you handle the transfer or sale of any Queensland real estate held by the deceased?
- **Complexity\:** Can you assist if a beneficiary challenges the will or makes a family provision claim?

You can also verify a solicitor's practising status and look for succession-law accreditation through the [Queensland Law Society](https://www.qls.com.au/)\.

**One important distinction\:** obtaining a grant of probate is only one part of the job. If you want help managing the estate from the initial asset and liability checks through to final distribution, make sure the engagement covers that broader work.
